title: [3.13] gh-149449: Fix use-after-free in `_PyUnicode_GetNameCAPI` (GH-150323) (#150354)
consumer: Objects/obmalloc.c (the freed block's pool); see the C-model sibling
live_proof: measured on the pinned 3.13.7 ASan build with PYTHONMALLOC=malloc and ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0: REGRESSION-TEST-FAILS. Running the trigger is the proof.
fidelity: interpreter-trigger, real allocator. Upstream's own reproducer driven through the real CPython. The SAME defect also exists in ../pymalloc-repros as a C model consumer against the same allocator; that one locates the faulting instruction with a labelled probe and this one does not, so for attribution the C model is the stronger of the two. This one exists because the C models cannot be built for the cheribsd-revocation arm at all: shared/corpus.h's inline asm uses "r" constraints that cannot hold a 128-bit capability.

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc stock on musl mallocng (tools/arms.json virtual-cpython): a fault in one of the case's fault_sites, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc's blocks as child lifetimes (patch 0014, CDERIVE/CREVOKE; tools/arms.json virtual-cpython-pools): as virtual-malloc
virtual-nested-pools.verdict_note: cause=25 pc=0x3fa42f2684 in PyCodec_NameReplaceErrors; by function: PyCodec_NameReplaceErrors is where host ASan reported the access

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completion while the block's arena stays live: pymalloc links the freed block onto its own pool free list, so the platform has no free to revoke. Once pymalloc returns an emptied arena to the system allocator (insert_to_freepool, when nf == ao->ntotalpools && ao->nextarena != NULL) the platform does have a free, and after a revocation sweep the stale access faults with SIGPROT si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG). Both outcomes are admissible; which one occurs depends on arena occupancy and sweep timing rather than on the defect, so this arm does not separate these cases. A bounds fault (si_code=1) would falsify this.

status: measured on three arms; matrix rows in results/20261006/matrix.tsv: spatial DETECTED cause=2 (not the mechanism) (spatial-20261007-020747); sublet DETECTED cause=24 (sublet-20261007-022142); cheribsd-revocation DETECTED si_code=5 (boundary-20261007-020413)
layer_note: unicodedata_create_capi (Modules/unicodedata.c:1465) takes the struct from PyMem_Malloc(sizeof(_PyUnicode_Name_CAPI)) = 16 bytes. The ASan nesting test cannot resolve this case because the fault is an indirect call through the dangling pointer -- ASan instruments loads and stores, not the jump, so it reports SEGV at the PC under PYTHONMALLOC unset and under PYTHONMALLOC=malloc alike. The routing was measured directly instead: PyMem_Malloc(16) freed and read back gives no ASan report with PYTHONMALLOC unset and heap-use-after-free with PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, so the MEM domain is pymalloc and 16 bytes is under the 512-byte threshold. PyMem_RawMalloc(16) reports in both, which is the control.
fault_sites_why: Host ASan (CPython 3.13.7 --with-address-sanitizer, PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, results/2026-10-10-asan/sites.tsv) reports heap-use-after-free (READ 8) at PyCodec_NameReplaceErrors Python/codecs.c:968. That run uses no Capstone arm and was recorded before any virtual arm ran.
note: The defect is two steps: the interpreter caches a pointer to _ucnhash_CAPI, a 16-byte PyMem_Malloc at Modules/unicodedata.c:1465; dropping the module frees the struct; the next \N{...} escape LOADS a function pointer out of the freed struct and CALLS it. The arms stop different steps. (2) is the detection: cause=25 INVALID_CAP on `ldc a4, 0x0(s2)`, the lifetime check rejecting the stale LOAD, in the declared fault site. The call is never reached. (1) WITHDRAWN as `D* 12`: the load is allowed and the MMU traps the CALL with cause=12, an instruction page fault. That is not a capability rule -- an ordinary non-CHERI CPU traps the same jump the same way. The faulting pc is `in ?` and MOVES between runs (...0b50c10 twice, then ...4a90c10) because it is not an address in the binary, it is the garbage that was called. (3) WITHDRAWN as `D* 5`: the load is allowed and the call fails the capability permission check, si_code=5 PROT_CHERI_PERM -- a capability rule, but not this arm's lifetime mechanism, which the guest's sicode selftest establishes as si_code=2 for a revoked access. (1) and (3) are therefore the same consequence under two different platform rules. This row read NO-READING until 2026-10-19: the judge cannot attribute a fault outside the declared fault_sites without a negative control, and the case had none. One was added -- the same two namereplace encodes, the same two compiles, the same del sys.modules['unicodedata'] and the same gc.collect(), with one extra reference held across the del so the struct is never freed -- and it runs to its end clean on both host builds while the trigger segfaults. See results caveat 4.
probe_why: trigger.py marks completion but not the access: its final print means the dangling CAPI was not caught, and nothing is printed at the moment it is used. That is what made the base arm's fault unattributable. probe-149449.py prints PRIMED, AT-ACCESS and PASSED around the first use, so a fault between the last two is that use. Added 2026-10-19.
probe_measured: Run 2026-10-19 on the pinned platform, both virtual arms print PRIMED then AT-ACCESS and neither prints PASSED, so the access is reached on both and neither allowed it to complete. The fault records separate the two arms far more sharply than the cause code alone. On base: cause=12 pc=0x3fa3610c30 address=0x3fa3610c30 with code=0x3fa2000000-0x3fa3000000 -- pc EQUALS address, which is the signature of an instruction fetch rather than a load or a store, and the pc lies OUTSIDE the code region, so the program jumped to an address that holds no code. On pools: cause=25 pc=0x3f962f2684 address=0x3f98590c10 with code=0x3f96000000-0x3f97000000 -- pc is inside the code region and differs from address, so a real instruction performed a load from a revoked capability. That is the mechanism on one arm and a jump into nothing on the other.
